findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` once, when the class body executes at module import. Every `AssignmentSource` that doesn't pass `queued` explicitly gets that same timestamp, which is the process start time. `from_integration` never passes it, so the field in the serialized `assignment_source_dict` is stale and useless for debugging or ordering. This is the classic dataclass mutable/dynamic default mistake. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The existing `test_to_dict` only checks `queued is not None`, so it passes with the bug.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to `sync_status_outbound` signature but never used
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter. Nothing in the PR passes it, reads it, or uses it for status sync, and concrete integrations are not updated. This widens the contract for no behavioural gain and suggests status sync is cycle-protected when it is not. Remove it, or implement and test the status-sync behaviour.

findings.title: Cycle-breaking tests cover only the assign path with a matching source
findings.body: Only `assign()` with a matching source integration is tested. Nothing covers `deassign(..., assignment_source=...)`, which is the path `sync_group_assignee_inbound` takes when `assign=False`. Nothing covers an `AssignmentSource` from a different integration still propagating outbound, which the comment in `should_sync` says must keep working. Nothing checks that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` attaches the source when it calls `assign`/`deassign`. The existing inbound tests don't mock outbound sync, so a regression in the wiring (the actual loop fix) would go unnoticed.
